title: Linear Time `list::size()` inside Loop Condition
pattern: Executing `collection.size()` or `.count()` inside a loop condition when the size check operation is non-constant-time.
why_bad: In older standard library implementations (like C++98 `std::list`), `size()` is O(N) because it counts elements sequentially, transforming a simple linear operation into an accidental O(N^2) algorithmic disaster.
detection: Loop termination conditions that repeatedly invoke a collection size method known to perform full traversals.
counterexample: Standard libraries where `size()` is guaranteed O(1).
fix: Maintain a manual count variable, check list emptiness (`empty()`), or use updated compilers with O(1) size tracking.
source: *The Art of Readable Code*, Chapter 5, "Example: list::size()" (p. 52 / 572).
